root_cause.text: mac80211's `ieee80211_parse_adv_t2l()` unconditionally consumed a TTLM link-map-presence byte even when the TTLM control flags indicated a default link mapping, but such elements omit that byte, causing out-of-bounds parsing.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE/commit states that “TTLM elements do not contain any link mapping presence indicator if a default mapping is used” and that mac80211 “would incorrectly parse the frame and would also read one byte beyond the end of the element”; the patch fixes this by making `link_map_presence = *pos; pos++;` conditional on `!(control & IEEE80211_TTLM_CONTROL_DEF_LINK_MAP)`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix T2L parsing to only consume the link map presence byte when an explicit link map is present rather than when the default link map flag is set.
intent_record.what: The code changed the unconditional read of `link_map_presence = *pos; pos++;` into a conditional block that executes only when `control` does not have the `IEEE80211_TTLM_CONTROL_DEF_LINK_MAP` flag set.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this prevents consuming a byte from the input buffer for `link_map_presence` when the default link map flag indicates that no explicit link map presence field is included, keeping parsing aligned with the frame format and avoiding incorrect parsing of subsequent fields.

relevance_review.reason: The change only updates the copyright year in the file header and does not affect TTLM parsing logic, control-flag handling, or bounds checking related to the out-of-bounds issue.

The change directly matches the root cause: it corrects T2L parsing so the link-map-presence byte is consumed only for explicit link maps, preventing the out-of-bounds parsing caused by treating default mapping as if that byte were present.

candidates.rationale: This unconditionally reads a link-map-presence byte from the buffer, even when the TTLM control flags indicate a default link mapping where no such byte is present, directly causing out-of-bounds parsing.
This advances the parser past a presumed link-map-presence byte unconditionally, misaligning subsequent parsing and contributing directly to out-of-bounds access when the byte is absent.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement unconditionally reads a link-map-presence byte from the current parse position, even when TTLM control flags indicate default link mapping and no such byte exists, causing out-of-bounds parsing.
This statement unconditionally advances past a presumed link-map-presence byte, which is absent for default link mapping, misaligning the parser and contributing to out-of-bounds access.

bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable logic is directly visible in `ieee80211_parse_adv_t2l()`. The root cause says the parser must not consume a `link-map-presence` byte when `IEEE80211_TTLM_CONTROL_DEF_LINK_MAP` is set, because default-link-mapping elements omit that byte. In this code, the parser always does `link_map_presence = *pos; pos++;` immediately after reading `control`, before checking `if (control & IEEE80211_TTLM_CONTROL_DEF_LINK_MAP)`. That means it unconditionally consumes one byte from `ttlm->optional` even for default-link-map elements. Only afterward does it handle the default-map case with `ttlm_info->map = 0xffff; return 0;`. This matches the stated root cause exactly: unconditional consumption of the link-map-presence byte prior to the DEF_LINK_MAP check, which can cause out-of-bounds parsing when that byte is absent. There is no fix present here, because the correct handling would be to check `IEEE80211_TTLM_CONTROL_DEF_LINK_MAP` before reading `link_map_presence`, or otherwise conditionally skip reading it.
